entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Marcus Pompeius Silvanus Staberius Flavianus, fully Marcus Pompeius Silvanus Staberius Flavinus or Flavianus, was a Roman senator who was consul twice.

Flavianus was born into a prominent senatorial family and rose to prominence in the late 1st century CE.

During his career, Flavianus played a key role in shaping Roman policy, particularly in the areas of foreign relations and domestic governance.

His significance extends beyond his own time, as he helped to lay the groundwork for the rise of the Flavian dynasty, which would go on to shape the course of Roman history.

The legacy of Flavianus can be seen in the many laws and policies he helped to enact, which had a lasting impact on the Roman Empire.

The Roman historian Tacitus wrote, 'Flavianus, the son of a senator, had the distinction of being consul twice, and of being the first of his family to attain the highest honors.'
